title: This Cambridge startup is building a ‘foundation model’ for the chest to speed drug trials
excerpt: Most AI imaging startups build one model per disease. A Cambridge company has raised $20m to build a single model for the whole chest. Then it can spin the rest out of that. content_html:
Most AI imaging startups build one model per disease. A Cambridge company has raised $20m to build a single model for the whole chest. Then it can spin the rest out of that.

Qureight makes AI imaging tools for lung and heart clinical trials. It closed a $20m Series B led by Molten Ventures, the company said. The round takes its total funding past €27m, Tech.eu reported.

The money builds an AI imaging lab around a general-purpose 3D model of the chest. From that base, Qureight says, it can build a disease-specific model in one or two months. From scratch, that takes about a year. It plans new models for asthma, lung cancer, pulmonary hypertension and bronchiectasis, on top of its existing lung-fibrosis work.

Its pitch to drugmakers centres on speed. One Qureight tool cuts imaging decisions in a trial from about two weeks to 48 hours. Another builds 3D maps of airways and blood vessels to track how a drug changes a disease. It even offers “synthetic control arms,” AI stand-ins for a real control group that can trim a trial’s cost.

AstraZeneca and Bristol Myers Squibb already use it, Tech Funding News reported. The market it is chasing, lung and heart trials, is forecast to reach $27.5bn by 2030.

The 💜 of EU tech

The latest rumblings from the EU tech scene, a story from our wise ol' founder Boris, and some questionable AI art. It's free, every week, in your inbox. Sign up now!

Two doctors and a CT scan

The origin story is unusual for an AI imaging firm. Two doctors, not engineers, founded Qureight in 2018. Chief executive Muhunthan Thillai is a chest physician who still sees patients, and he started it after a CT scan he could not confidently read.

To cover the gap, the founders hired a senior technical bench. It includes a former global platform head at HP and a machine-learning professor from Imperial College London. Its closest European rival, Oxford’s Brainomix, sells diagnostic software to hospitals. Qureight sits earlier, inside the trial itself.

Keeping it in London

The raise says something about where AI-in-medicine money now flows. Qureight approached Molten two years ago, and Molten said no. This time three investors sent term sheets in six weeks. It turned down US offers to keep the round with a London fund.

This is the same rush of capital chasing AI for drug discovery and AI biology. A run of health-tech raises sits alongside it. Qureight plans to double its staff to 100 by December. Whether its chest model becomes a trial standard or stays a niche tool depends on the partnerships it lands next.

content_html_zh:
大多数人工智能成像初创公司都会为每种疾病构建一个模型。 剑桥的一家公司已筹集 2000 万美元，用于打造整个胸部的单一模型。 然后它就可以将剩下的部分剥离出来。

Qureight 为肺和心脏临床试验开发人工智能成像工具。 该公司表示，它完成了由 Molten Ventures 领投的 2000 万美元 B 轮融资。 据 Tech.eu 报道，本轮融资总额超过 2700 万欧元。

这笔资金围绕通用的胸部 3D 模型建立了一个人工智能成像实验室。 奎赖特说，以此为基础，它可以在一两个月内建立一个特定疾病的模型。 从零开始，大约需要一年的时间。 在现有的肺纤维化研究基础上，该公司计划开发治疗哮喘、肺癌、肺动脉高压和支气管扩张的新模型。

它向制药商推销的重点是速度。 一款 Qureight 工具可将试验中的成像决策从大约两周缩短到 48 小时。 另一个构建气道和血管的 3D 地图来跟踪药物如何改变疾病。 它甚至提供“合成控制臂”，即真实对照组的人工智能替代品，可以降低试验成本。

据科技资助新闻报道，阿斯利康和百时美施贵宝已经在使用它。 它所追逐的肺和心脏试验市场预计到 2030 年将达到 275 亿美元。

欧盟科技的💜

来自欧盟科技界的最新传言、我们明智的创始人鲍里斯的故事，以及一些值得怀疑的人工智能艺术。 每周都会免费发送到您的收件箱中。 立即注册！

两名医生和 CT 扫描

对于一家人工智能成像公司来说，这个起源故事并不寻常。 Qureight 于 2018 年由两名医生而非工程师创立。 首席执行官穆亨坦·蒂莱 (Muhunthan Thillai) 是一名胸科医师，仍在为病人看诊，他在无法自信地读取 CT 扫描后开始了这项工作。

为了弥补这一差距，创始人聘请了一名高级技术人员。 其中包括惠普前全球平台主管和伦敦帝国理工学院的机器学习教授。 它最接近的欧洲竞争对手是牛津大学的 Brainomix，向医院销售诊断软件。 奎赖特坐在较早的位置，在审判现场。

保留在伦敦

此次融资说明了人工智能医疗资金现在的流向。 两年前，Qureight 曾与 Molten 接洽，但被 Molten 拒绝了。 这次，三名投资者在六周内发送了投资意向书。 它拒绝了美国提出的由伦敦基金继续该轮融资的提议。

这与资本追逐人工智能用于药物发现和人工智能生物学的热潮是一样的。 与此同时，一系列健康技术领域的加薪也随之而来。 Qureight 计划到 12 月将员工人数增加一倍，达到 100 人。 它的胸部模型是否成为试用标准或仍然是一个小众工具取决于它接下来获得的合作伙伴。
